key_insight: A domain-focused continual pretraining corpus (11.8B tokens from 28.6K curated cybersecurity documents) enables an open, privacy-preserving generalist LLM tailored to real-world security workflows.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between privacy-risky proprietary API assistants and generic open models by adapting an LLM specifically for diverse cybersecurity tasks without exposing sensitive data.
method: Large-scale web filtering plus manual collection to assemble 11.8B tokens spanning frameworks, offensive techniques, and security tools (28.6K documents).
Continual pretraining of an LLM on the curated cybersecurity corpus to produce a domain-adapted generalist model.
Design for privacy-preserving deployment to avoid reliance on proprietary APIs while supporting diverse security workflows.
impact: Provides AI/ML and security teams with an open, specialized assistant that understands security context and can be deployed privately—reducing exposure of sensitive telemetry to third-party services.
visual_elements: Dataset pipeline diagram: web crawl → automated filtering → manual curation → final corpus (11.8B tokens, 28.6K docs).
Model training flow: base LLM → continual pretraining → cybersecurity-adapted generalist.
Workflow icons: incident response, threat hunting, vulnerability analysis, and tool automation to show applied use cases.
Privacy comparison graphic: on-prem/local deployment (shield) vs proprietary API (cloud lock) highlighting reduced data exposure.
paper_authors: Naufal Suryanto, Muzammal Naseer, Pengfei Li, Syed Talal Wasim, Jinhui Yi
